title: HOW TO BECOME A PROFESSIONAL BUSINESS ANALYST
nextLesson: BUSINESS ANALYSIS FUNDAMENTALS: HOW TO GATHER AND DOCUMENT REQUIREMENTS

o: To write computer code for every project
To understand business problems and help identify suitable solutions
To manage every employee in an organisation
questions.q: What is the primary role of a business analyst?
questions.good: Correct! A business analyst helps organisations understand problems and identify appropriate solutions.
questions.hint: Think about the person who connects business needs with solutions.
questions.review: The role and purpose of a business analyst.

o: People affected by a project or interested in its outcome
questions.good: Excellent! Stakeholders can include customers, employees, managers, suppliers and developers.
questions.hint: Think about everyone who has an interest in the project.

o: Investigate the problem and collect reliable information
questions.q: What should a business analyst do before recommending a solution?
questions.good: Correct! Understanding the real problem comes before choosing a solution.
questions.hint: Do not guess. Find out what is actually happening.

o: The needs or conditions a business or its users expect a solution to satisfy
questions.good: Well done! Requirements describe what the business or users need from a solution.
questions.hint: They explain what the solution must provide.

o: To show the steps involved in a business process
questions.q: What is the purpose of process mapping?
questions.good: Correct! Process maps help people understand how work moves through a business.
questions.hint: Think about showing a process from its beginning to its end.

o: AS-IS means future, while TO-BE means past
AS-IS describes the current process, while TO-BE describes the desired future process
Both terms mean exactly the same thing
questions.q: What is the difference between AS-IS and TO-BE?
questions.good: Excellent! AS-IS shows the current situation, while TO-BE shows the intended improvement.
questions.hint: One describes what happens now; the other describes what should happen.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an essential business analyst skill?
questions.good: Correct! Analytical thinking and problem-solving help analysts understand issues and recommend solutions.
questions.hint: Think about the skills needed to investigate a business problem.
questions.review: Communication, analysis, problem-solving and attention to detail.

questions.q: Which tool is commonly used for managing project work and requirements?
questions.good: Right! Jira is commonly used by teams to manage project work and track requirements.
questions.hint: It is a project and issue-tracking tool.
questions.review: Common business analysis tools and their uses.

o: To demonstrate practical skills and problem-solving ability
questions.q: Why should a beginner business analyst build a portfolio?
questions.good: Excellent! A portfolio gives employers examples of how you approach and document business problems.
questions.hint: Think about how you can prove what you are capable of doing.
questions.review: Practical projects, experience and portfolio development.

o: Stop learning after receiving a certificate
Continue learning, practise with real problems and build professional experience
questions.q: Which approach best supports a successful business analyst career?
questions.good: Correct! A professional business analyst keeps improving, gains experience and adapts to changing business needs.
questions.hint: Professional growth requires continuous learning and practical experience.
questions.review: Building a sustainable business analyst career.

announcements.text: Learning objective | By the end of this lesson, you should understand what a business analyst does, the essential skills required, the tools used in the profession and how to begin your career.
Identify one everyday business problem and write down how you would investigate it and recommend a solution.

disclaimer: This lesson is for educational purposes. Professional business analysis requires continuous learning, practical experience and adaptation to each organisation.
